justifications.functional_suitability: Core elements like Real-Time Scoring Engine and Case Management Service are present, but vital interactions are missing: no relationship connects the Scoring Engine to Case Management for review cases, nor connects Model Management Service to the Scoring Engine for zero-downtime updates.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Local IPC and Redis queues support low latency, but synchronously invoking Tokenization Proxy (backed by AWS KMS/CloudHSM) on the critical authorization path creates significant latency and throughput bottlenecks under 3,000 req/s with a sub-50ms P99 target.
justifications.compatibility: The Scoring Gateway Controller natively supports standard REST API over TLS 1.3 for Payment Gateways, and the Authentication & RBAC Manager integrates standard OIDC/OAuth2 protocols for analyst identity.
justifications.usability: The Case Management Service provides a dedicated Web Interface with Cognito RBAC for Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers, alongside explainability views in Model Management Service, satisfying primary user interaction needs.
justifications.reliability: Although the Audit Sidecar includes a local buffer, there is no explicit fail-open or bypass mechanism specified in the Scoring Gateway Controller to guarantee payments are unblocked within 1 minute if scoring components fail.
justifications.security: Security is addressed thoroughly: Tokenization Proxy with CloudHSM/KMS isolates PANs, gRPC uses mTLS, Cognito manages RBAC, and Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar writes signed logs to Amazon S3 WORM buckets for 7-year tamper resistance.
justifications.maintainability: Responsibilities are modularly divided into dedicated containers (Scoring, Tokenization, Case Management, Auditing). However, missing integration channels between Model Promotion Controller and the Scoring Engine leave runtime update maintenance underspecified.
justifications.portability: The design matches the specified AWS target environment using ECS Fargate containers, although heavy reliance on proprietary AWS services (Cognito, CloudHSM, KMS, X-Ray) limits portability across alternative cloud providers.

PERF-01.justification: While local IPC to the sidecar avoids network hops, synchronous tokenization via Tokenization Proxy calling CloudHSM and KMS per authorization risks exceeding the 50 ms P99 threshold at 3,000 RPS.
sensitivity_points: Synchronous cryptographic calls to CloudHSM and KMS on the critical path.
tradeoffs: Strong format-preserving tokenization security traded against transaction scoring latency.

PERF-02.justification: Case management runs as a distinct ECS service using Amazon Redis for queue state and S3 for storage, completely isolated from real-time scoring runtime resources.
sensitivity_points: Strict process and network separation between scoring workload and case management queries.
tradeoffs: Deploying independent services increases operational complexity for a small three-engineer team.

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture lacks an explicit gateway fallback or circuit-breaking mechanism to automatically bypass or default-decision payments and record audits when the Real-Time Scoring Engine container crashes.
sensitivity_points: Absence of edge-level circuit breaker or standalone fail-open fallback path.
tradeoffs: Centralizing scoring logic in one engine avoids dual maintenance but creates single-point-of-failure risks.

AVAIL-02.justification: The Audit Sidecar buffers log batches to local encrypted tmpfs and EBS storage via asynchronous IPC, shielding scoring latency from downstream S3 or KMS delays.
sensitivity_points: Local buffer capacity during prolonged S3 WORM or KMS outages.
tradeoffs: Local asynchronous buffering ensures sub-50ms latency but introduces transient durability exposure before flush.

MOD-01.justification: Model Promotion Controller supports promotion and rollback via version manifests in S3, and memory-cached models enable zero downtime, though hot-reloading mechanism details are implicit.
sensitivity_points: Synchronization latency when propagating updated model manifests to active scoring instances.
tradeoffs: In-memory model caching maximizes evaluation throughput at the expense of runtime cache invalidation.

MOD-02.justification: The model service supports versioning, but the architecture omits a distributed state store for real-time velocity calculations across distributed scoring instances.
sensitivity_points: Lack of shared low-latency state store for multi-instance velocity counter tracking.
tradeoffs: Stateless scoring nodes maximize raw compute speed but constrain complex velocity rule evaluation.

SEC-01.justification: Card numbers are tokenized and analysts access cases via Cognito RBAC, preventing PAN visibility, but anomalous analyst access detection and 15-minute alerting mechanisms are missing.
sensitivity_points: Absence of dedicated user behavior analytics or automated security alerting pipelines.
tradeoffs: Relying on standard IAM and Cognito simplifies maintenance but limits automated intrusion response.

SEC-02.justification: Audit logs and model manifests are stored in S3 WORM with Glacier Instant Retrieval for 7 years, while Explainability Previewer can reproduce historic decisions.
sensitivity_points: Long-term immutability and retrievability of S3 Object Lock storage.
tradeoffs: Glacier Instant Retrieval maintains fast query response times under tight long-term storage budgets.
